A 25-year-old woman returns to the clinic for follow-up on her AIDS treatment with highly active
antiretroviral therapy (HAART). She is in good spirits, adherent to her medications and clinic visits, and
is also taking prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Recent lab results reveal the following: |
Hemoglobin | 11 g/dL | | --- | --- | | Mean corpuscular volume | 80 fL | | Reticulocyte count | 0.5% | |
Erythrocyte count | 2 × 10■/mm³ | | Leukocyte count | 700/mm³ | | Neutrophils | 40% | | Platelet count |
20,000/mm³ | Additional tests show decreased viral DNA, reduced mRNA burden, and a significantly

lower viral load. To avoid altering her effective antiretroviral therapy, she is started on a medication to
improve her blood cell counts. Thirty minutes after receiving the first dose, she develops symptoms
including difficulty breathing, severe muscle pain, vomiting, a pulse of 104/min, and a blood pressure of
82/54 mm Hg. Which of the following medications was most likely given to this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) Platelet-derived growth factor (B) Pegfilgrastim (C) Filgrastim (D) Oprelvekin (E)
Lenograstim (F) Sargramostim (G) Interleukin-11 (H) Thrombopoietin (I) Erythropoietin (J) Romiplostim
 A. Erythropoietin
B. Platelet-derived growth factor
C. Romiplostim
D. Filgrastim
